scenes.visual: Title card: model + harness = coding agent
scenes.text: Every coding agent is really two things: a model, and a harness. The harness is the tools, the prompts and the loop that turn a model into an engineer. Tools like OpenCode let you swap the model. But the harness matters just as much.

scenes.visual: Harness terminals appear one by one
scenes.text: Claude Code. Codex. Qwen Code. MiniMax. Gemini CLI. Each has its own strengths, its own quirks, and its own fans. And each one is a separate install, a separate login, a separate terminal to babysit.

So we built OpenHarness. Think of it as OpenCode, but for harnesses: one web coding agent where you pick the harness and the model, for whatever reason matters to you. Ten harnesses, more than sixty models, powered by HarnessRouter.

scenes.visual: Try the demo, pick repo, pick Qwen Code, pick qwen3.8-max, type the task, run
scenes.text: Sign in, or try the demo, and pick a repository. Here it's mitt, a tiny event emitter. Choose the harness: Qwen Code. Then the model. Qwen Code can run sixty of them, from Qwen and DeepSeek to Claude and GPT. We'll take Qwen 3.8 Max. Describe the task, and run it.

scenes.visual: Session view streaming live steps (sped up)
scenes.text: OpenHarness streams the harness's work as it happens: every command, every edit. The agent runs in an isolated HarnessRouter sandbox. It clones the repo, reads the code, runs the existing tests, writes the change, and checks its own work. This run took seventeen minutes, so we've sped it up.

scenes.visual: Result card, tests passed, diff viewer, summary
scenes.text: When it's done, you get something you can review: a summary, the test status, the full diff, and exactly what it cost. Qwen Code added the method with ten new tests, all passing, plus README docs, for about a dollar twenty.

scenes.visual: Follow-up question in the same session
scenes.text: Questions about the change? Just follow up in the same session. The harness keeps its full context, so it can explain exactly how its code behaves, like why a handler that emits its own event still fires only once.

scenes.visual: Race setup: Qwen Code on qwen3.8-max vs Codex on gpt-6-luna
scenes.text: And with every harness one click away, you can even run them side by side. Same task: Qwen Code on Qwen 3.8 Max, and Codex running GPT-6 Luna.

scenes.visual: Race live (sped up) and results with Fastest/Cheapest badges
scenes.text: Codex finished in under five minutes for three cents, but couldn't run the project's old test suite. Qwen Code took longer, worked around it, and got all twenty-eight tests passing. Speed, cost, thoroughness, or just the harness you like working with: the choice is yours, task by task.

Under the hood, our Next.js backend owns sign-in, sessions and repo access. It calls HarnessRouter's Responses API, with one harness per agent base and the model chosen per task. API keys and harness IDs never reach the browser.
OpenHarness. Any harness. Any model. Your choice.
